newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on weak sentiment.

text.p: Taiwan stocks are expected to continue a consolidation on Wednesday as a row over the government's ability to fight crime is likely to intensify after a second teenager's kidnap and murder, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the weighted index closed 14.52 points or 0.18 percent lower at 7,952.12.
The scheduled announcement of a partial cabinet reshuffle in Wednesday morning was unlikely to inspire buying interest, brokers said.
"Even though the latest kidnap and murder case does not involve celebrity, it reaffairms Taiwan's law and order is indeed declining," said Tsao Chung-ping, an analyst of Ting Kong Securities.
Police said on Tuesday Tsai Chin-hsin, 15-year-old son of a local businessman, was murdered by his abductors before police or his parents could respond.

Many people were not satisfied with the cabinet reshuffle list, which was expected to be announced during a ruling Party's meeting. "The list leaked by local media is not impressive at all," Tsao said.
